0001| #!/bin/sh
0002| # Forgel Code installer.
0003| #
0004| # One command installs the client into a per-user prefix:
0005| #
0006| #   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0007| #
0008| # The client goes into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}, the
0009| # ``forgel-code`` launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, and that
0010| # directory is put on PATH through one marked block in the profile an
0011| # interactive login session of the login shell reads. The login shell is taken
0012| # from $SHELL, then from the invoking process (ps), then from the account login
0013| # shell; a shell outside the zsh and bash families gets the block in
0014| # $HOME/.profile and a warning that names the edited file. After writing the
0015| # block the installer starts that shell as a login interactive shell from a
0016| # cleared environment, in a process group of its own, under a hard time limit.
0017| # A watchdog stops that shell once the limit elapses, and the installer times
0018| # the check itself: a shell that outlived the limit fails the installation,
0019| # whatever the ordering of its own exit and the watchdog's timeout record. The
0020| # absence of a recorded timeout at the moment the check's result arrives is
0021| # never taken as evidence that the check kept its bound. Nothing the check
0022| # started outlives it: the dedicated group, and the descendants that left it,
0023| # are stopped on every exit path. The installer then checks that
0024| # ``forgel-code`` resolves to the launcher it just wrote. Re-running replaces
0025| # the installation; running with ``--uninstall`` removes it again.
0026| #
0027| # Installing the client alone is not enough to use it, so the same run also
0028| # makes sure an engine the client supports is in place. It asks the engine's own
0029| # installer which version the configured engine source provides, without
0030| # installing anything, and reads the version of an engine that is already
0031| # present. Only then does it decide: a present engine that satisfies the
0032| # client's minimum is kept when the available version is not strictly newer, a
0033| # strictly newer available engine replaces it, and an absent engine is obtained
0034| # when the available version is supported. Anything else ends the run as a
0035| # failure that names the required minimum, the version found or offered and the
0036| # action the user can take. A successful run always states the engine version in
0037| # place and how it was obtained. ``--client-only`` installs the client alone and
0038| # touches no engine. Reading a version report, and installing a version, are the
0039| # engine installer's own jobs; this script only decides and delegates.
0040| #
0041| # Environment variables:
0042| #   FORGEL_CODE_HOME            install prefix (default: $HOME/.local/share/forgel-code)
0043| #   FORGEL_CODE_BIN             launcher directory (default: $HOME/.local/bin)
0044| #   FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE          local checkout to install from, without network
0045| #   FORGEL_CODE_TAG             repository tag when no checkout is given (default: v0.2.0)
0046| #   FORGEL_CODE_REPOSITORY      repository URL used with FORGEL_CODE_TAG
0047| #   FORGEL_CODE_PYTHON          Python 3 interpreter (default: python3 on PATH)
0048| #   FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE         shell profile to edit (default: chosen from the login shell)
0049| #   FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH  set to leave the shell profile untouched
0050| #   FORGEL_CODE_NO_PROFILE_EDIT the same opt-out under its older name
0051| #   FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT         seconds the fresh-shell check may take (default: 10)
0052| #   FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE        engine source the engine installer resolves against
0053| #                               (default: https://github.com/forgel-dev/forgel)
0054| #   FORGEL_ENGINE_INSTALLER     the engine's own installer (default: forgel-install on PATH)
0055| #   FORGEL_ENGINE               engine binary whose version is read (default: forgel on PATH)
0056| #
0057| # The script is POSIX ``sh`` and safe to pipe into: it never reads stdin.
0058| 
0059| set -eu
0060| 
0061| # The exact markers an uninstall looks for. They are compared byte for byte.
0062| MARKER_START='# >>> forgel-code >>>'
0063| MARKER_END='# <<< forgel-code <<<'
0064| 
0065| # A profile whose last line has no final newline cannot be restored byte for
0066| # byte from the block alone: the newline that separates that line from the
0067| # block is indistinguishable from one the file always had. The installer
0068| # records the case in one comment line directly above the block and removes
0069| # that line, with the separator newline, together with the block.
0070| MARKER_SEPARATOR='# forgel-code: the line above had no final newline'
0071| 
0072| HOME_DIR=${HOME:-/}
0073| PREFIX=${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME_DIR/.local/share/forgel-code}
0074| BIN_DIR=${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME_DIR/.local/bin}
0075| LAUNCHER=$BIN_DIR/forgel-code
0076| TAG=${FORGEL_CODE_TAG:-v0.2.0}
0077| REPOSITORY=${FORGEL_CODE_REPOSITORY:-https://github.com/forgel-dev/code}
0078| 
0079| # The engine side of the installation: the source the run asks about, the
0080| # engine's own installer that answers and installs, and the binary whose version
0081| # report says what is already in place.
0082| ENGINE_SOURCE=${FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE:-https://github.com/forgel-dev/forgel}
0083| ENGINE_INSTALLER=${FORGEL_ENGINE_INSTALLER:-forgel-install}
0084| 
0085| # What the engine part of the run learned, filled in before anything is decided.
0086| # A failure report quotes whichever of them are known.
0087| ENGINE_MINIMUM=
0088| ENGINE_PRESENT=
0089| ENGINE_AVAILABLE=
0090| 
0091| # What a fresh shell reports back: its own PATH and the path it resolves
0092| # ``forgel-code`` to. The prefixes keep the answer readable next to anything a
0093| # system-wide profile may print.
0094| CHECK_PATH=/usr/bin:/bin
0095| CHECK_COMMAND='printf "forgel-fresh-path=%s\n" "$PATH"; fresh=$(command -v forgel-code || true); printf "forgel-fresh-resolved=%s\n" "$fresh"'
0096| 
0097| # The bound for the fresh-shell check, in seconds, when FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT is
0098| # unset, and the grace period the checked shell gets between the graceful stop
0099| # and the forceful one. A login shell reads its startup files in milliseconds;
0100| # ten seconds leaves room on a slow machine and still bounds a shell that never
0101| # answers.
0102| DEFAULT_VERIFY_LIMIT=10
0103| VERIFY_GRACE=2
0104| 
0105| # How long the installer waits for the watchdog's decision, in whole seconds,
0106| # derived from the grace period. One polling step of the watchdog is the longest
0107| # the decision can take after the checked command exits, so one grace period
0108| # covers it with room to spare. A watchdog that never answers cannot hold the
0109| # installer longer than this.
0110| DECISION_WAIT=$VERIFY_GRACE
0111| if [ "$DECISION_WAIT" -lt 1 ]; then
0112|     DECISION_WAIT=1
0113| fi
0114| 
0115| # The profile files this installer can have written. ``--uninstall`` cleans the
0116| # block out of every one of them, so no stale PATH entry stays behind. The list
0117| # is a superset of what the install path may edit, including ~/.bashrc, because
0118| # a non-login bash session reads that file and an earlier installation could
0119| # have left its block there.
0120| PROFILE_NAMES='.zshrc .zprofile .zshenv .bash_profile .bash_login .profile .bashrc'
0121| 
0122| # Set by ``verify_profile`` once the fresh shell resolved the launcher.
0123| VERIFIED_PATH=
0124| 
0125| # What the bounded check owns while it runs: its private directory, the command
0126| # it started, the process group that command leads and the watchdog that bounds
0127| # it. Every one of them is released by ``cleanup_check``, whichever way the
0128| # script ends.
0129| CHECK_DIR=
0130| CHECK_CHILD=
0131| CHECK_GROUP=
0132| CHECK_WATCHER=
0133| 
0134| # Set by ``cleanup_check`` once the current check has been released, so the exit
0135| # trap and a signal trap cannot release the same check twice.
0136| CHECK_CLEANED=
0137| 
0138| # Set by ``bounded_run``: the exit status of the checked command and what it
0139| # printed. A status of 124 means the bound elapsed.
0140| CHECK_STATUS=0
0141| CHECK_OUTPUT=
0142| 
0143| # How two engine versions are ordered. The ordering is numeric component by
0144| # component, ignores one leading version marker and trailing zero components, so
0145| # ``v0.2.0``, ``0.2`` and ``0.2.0.0`` are the same version. A version with a
0146| # component that is not a number cannot be ordered at all: the helper exits with
0147| # status 2 and the caller treats that version as not satisfying a minimum.
0148| # ``ge`` and ``gt`` compare; both exit 0 only for a true answer.
0149| VERSION_HELPER='
0150| import sys
0151| 
0152| def parse(text):
0153|     text = text.strip()
0154|     if text[:1] in ("v", "V"):
0155|         text = text[1:]
0156|     if not text:
0157|         return None
0158|     numbers = []
0159|     for part in text.split("."):
0160|         if not part.isdigit() or not part.isascii():
0161|             return None
0162|         numbers.append(int(part))
0163|     while len(numbers) > 1 and numbers[-1] == 0:
0164|         numbers.pop()
0165|     return numbers
0166| 
0167| if len(sys.argv) < 4:
0168|     sys.exit(2)
0169| operator, left, right = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
0170| first = parse(left)
0171| second = parse(right)
0172| if first is None or second is None:
0173|     sys.exit(2)
0174| width = max(len(first), len(second))
0175| first = first + [0] * (width - len(first))
0176| second = second + [0] * (width - len(second))
0177| if operator == "ge":
0178|     sys.exit(0 if first >= second else 1)
0179| if operator == "gt":
0180|     sys.exit(0 if first > second else 1)
0181| sys.exit(2)
0182| '
0183| 
0184| usage() {
0185|     cat <<'USAGE'
0186| Usage: install.sh [--client-only] [--uninstall] [--help]
0187| 
0188| Installs the Forgel Code client into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}
0189| and its launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, adding that directory
0190| to PATH with one marked block in the profile the login shell reads. The result
0191| is checked in a freshly started login interactive shell under a bounded time
0192| limit. The same run also makes sure an engine the client supports is in place,
0193| and states which engine version it ended with and how it was obtained.
0194| 
0195|   --client-only  install the client alone and leave any engine untouched
0196|   --uninstall    remove the installation, the launcher and the PATH block
0197|   --help         show this text
0198| 
0199| The engine source is ${FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE:-https://github.com/forgel-dev/forgel}
0200| and the engine's own installer is ${FORGEL_ENGINE_INSTALLER:-forgel-install} on PATH;

0001| """Run the Forgel engine as a separate process and read its JSON answer.
0002| 
0003| The client never imports the engine. The only channel is
0004| ``forgel <command> --json`` executed as a child process whose stdout holds one
0005| JSON object.
0006| """
0007| 
0008| from __future__ import annotations
0009| 
0010| import json
0011| import subprocess
0012| from typing import Any, Dict, Optional, Sequence
0013| 
0014| # Seconds to wait for one engine call before giving up. ``--timeout`` and
0015| # ``$FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT`` override it.
0016| DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 600.0
0017| 
0018| # How much of an unreadable engine answer an error message quotes.
0019| EXCERPT_LIMIT = 300
0020| 
0021| # Exit code the client uses when the engine did not answer in time.
0022| TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE = 124
0023| 
0024| 
0025| def _format_seconds(value: float) -> str:
0026|     return "%g" % float(value)
0027| 
0028| 
0029| def _excerpt(text: str) -> str:
0030|     """A bounded, single-line excerpt of what the engine printed."""
0031|     flat = " ".join(text.split())
0032|     if len(flat) <= EXCERPT_LIMIT:
0033|         return flat
0034|     return flat[:EXCERPT_LIMIT] + "..."
0035| 
0036| 
0037| def _structured_message(error: Any) -> str:
0038|     """Render the engine's structured error fields without inventing any."""
0039|     if isinstance(error, str):
0040|         return error.strip()
0041|     if isinstance(error, dict):
0042|         parts = []
0043|         for key in ("code", "kind", "message"):
0044|             if error.get(key) is not None:
0045|                 parts.append("%s=%s" % (key, error[key]))
0046|         for key in sorted(error):
0047|             if key in ("code", "kind", "message"):
0048|                 continue
0049|             value = error[key]
0050|             if isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)) and value != "":
0051|                 parts.append("%s=%s" % (key, value))
0052|         if parts:
0053|             return "engine reported " + ", ".join(parts)
0054|         return "engine reported an empty error"
0055|     if error is None:
0056|         return ""
0057|     return json.dumps(error, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)
0058| 
0059| 
0060| class EngineError(Exception):
0061|     """The engine failed or answered with something the client cannot read."""
0062| 
0063|     def __init__(
0064|         self,
0065|         message: str,
0066|         returncode: int = 1,
0067|         payload: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
0068|     ) -> None:
0069|         super().__init__(message)
0070|         self.message = message
0071|         self.returncode = returncode
0072|         # The engine's own structured error object, when it supplied one.
0073|         self.payload = payload
0074| 
0075| 
0076| def parse_json_object(output: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
0077|     """Return the JSON object the engine printed, wherever it starts.
0078| 
0079|     The first decodable JSON object in the output wins: a log line that merely
0080|     contains ``{`` must not make the real answer unreadable.
0081|     """
0082|     text = output.strip()
0083|     if not text:
0084|         raise EngineError("engine printed no output")
0085| 
0086|     try:
0087|         whole = json.loads(text)
0088|     except json.JSONDecodeError:
0089|         whole = None
0090|     if isinstance(whole, dict):
0091|         return whole
0092|     if whole is not None:
0093|         raise EngineError(
0094|             "engine printed a JSON value that is not an object: %s" % _excerpt(text)
0095|         )
0096| 
0097|     decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
0098|     index = text.find("{")
0099|     while index >= 0:
0100|         try:
0101|             candidate, _end = decoder.raw_decode(text[index:])
0102|         except json.JSONDecodeError:
0103|             candidate = None
0104|         if isinstance(candidate, dict):
0105|             return candidate
0106|         index = text.find("{", index + 1)
0107|     raise EngineError(
0108|         "engine printed no JSON object; received: %s" % _excerpt(text)
0109|     )
0110| 
0111| 
0112| class Engine:
0113|     """A handle on the ``forgel`` executable."""
0114| 
0115|     def __init__(self, binary: str = "forgel", timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT) -> None:
0116|         self.binary = binary
0117|         self.timeout = float(timeout)
0118| 
0119|     def label(self) -> str:
0120|         """How this engine is named in a report: its identity is its path."""
0121|         return "engine %s" % self.binary
0122| 
0123|     def failure(
0124|         self,
0125|         detail: str,
0126|         returncode: int,
0127|         payload: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
0128|     ) -> "EngineError":
0129|         """An engine error that names the engine which failed."""
0130|         return EngineError(
0131|             "%s: %s" % (self.label(), detail), returncode, payload
0132|         )
0133| 
0134|     def command(self, arguments: Sequence[str]) -> list:
0135|         """Return the child argv: ``forgel <command> --json``."""
0136|         return [self.binary, *arguments, "--json"]
0137| 
0138|     def run(self, arguments: Sequence[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
0139|         """Run one engine command and return its JSON object."""
0140|         argv = self.command(arguments)
0141|         try:
0142|             completed = subprocess.run(
0143|                 argv,
0144|                 stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
0145|                 capture_output=True,
0146|                 timeout=self.timeout,
0147|             )
0148|         except FileNotFoundError:
0149|             raise self.failure(
0150|                 "executable not found: %s" % self.binary, 127
0151|             ) from None
0152|         except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
0153|             raise self.failure(
0154|                 "timed out after %s seconds"
0155|                 % _format_seconds(self.timeout),
0156|                 TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE,
0157|             ) from None
0158|         except OSError as exc:
0159|             raise self.failure("cannot run: %s" % exc, 126) from None
0160| 
0161|         # The engine always speaks UTF-8; the process locale must not matter.
0162|         stdout = completed.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")
0163|         stderr = completed.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace")
0164| 
0165|         payload: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
0166|         unreadable: Optional[EngineError] = None
0167|         try:
0168|             payload = parse_json_object(stdout)
0169|         except EngineError as exc:
0170|             unreadable = exc
0171| 
0172|         returncode = completed.returncode
0173|         if returncode != 0:
0174|             error = payload.get("error") if payload is not None else None
0175|             if error is not None:
0176|                 message = _structured_message(error)
0177|                 fields = error if isinstance(error, dict) else None
0178|             else:
0179|                 message = stderr.strip() or stdout.strip()
0180|                 if not message:
0181|                     message = "exited with code %d" % returncode
0182|                 fields = None
0183|             raise self.failure(message, returncode or 1, fields)
0184| 
0185|         if payload is None:
0186|             message = (
0187|                 unreadable.message
0188|                 if unreadable is not None
0189|                 else "printed no output"
0190|             )
0191|             raise self.failure(message, 1)
0192| 
0193|         if payload.get("ok") is False:
0194|             # A structured refusal is a failure even when the engine exited 0,
0195|             # and its own fields are carried through instead of raw output.
0196|             error = payload.get("error")
0197|             if error is not None:
0198|                 message = _structured_message(error)
0199|             else:
0200|                 message = stderr.strip() or stdout.strip() or "reported ok=false"
0201|             raise self.failure(
0202|                 message, 1, error if isinstance(error, dict) else None
0203|             )
0204| 
0205|         return payload

0023| class EngineCase(InstallerCase):
0024|     """A scenario with a present engine it can place and inspect."""
0025| 
0026|     def setUp(self) -> None:
0027|         super().setUp()
0028|         self.log_path = self.env["FORGEL_STUB_ENGINE_LOG"]
0029|         self.clear_log()
0030| 
0031|     def offer(self, version: str) -> None:
0032|         """The version the configured engine source offers in this scenario."""
0033|         self.env["FORGEL_STUB_ENGINE_AVAILABLE"] = version
0034| 
0035|     def clear_log(self) -> None:
0036|         if os.path.exists(self.log_path):
0037|             os.remove(self.log_path)
0038| 
0039|     def calls(self):
0040|         """Every argv the stand-in for the engine's installer received."""
0041|         if not os.path.exists(self.log_path):
0042|             return []
0043|         with open(self.log_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
0044|             return [json.loads(line) for line in handle if line.strip()]
0045| 
0046|     def install_calls(self):
0047|         """The recorded calls that asked for a version to be installed."""
0048|         found = []
0049|         for argv in self.calls():
0050|             for argument in argv:
0051|                 if argument == "--install" or argument.startswith("--install="):
0052|                     found.append(argv)
0053|                     break
0054|         return found
0055| 
0056|     def preinstall(self, version: str) -> None:
0057|         """Place an engine at ``version``, as an earlier installation would."""
0058|         directory = os.path.dirname(self.env["FORGEL_ENGINE"])
0059|         if directory:
0060|             os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
0061|         result = _run(
0062|             [
0063|                 self.env["FORGEL_ENGINE_INSTALLER"],
0064|                 "--source",
0065|                 "test",
0066|                 "--install",
0067|                 version,
0068|             ],
0069|             self.base,
0070|             self.env,
0071|         )
0072|         self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
0073|         self.clear_log()
0074| 
0075|     def engine_version(self) -> str:
0076|         """The version the engine in place reports, or ``""`` when absent."""
0077|         if not os.path.exists(self.env["FORGEL_ENGINE"]):
0078|             return ""
0079|         result = _run(
0080|             [self.env["FORGEL_ENGINE"], "--version", "--json"], self.base, self.env
0081|         )
0082|         self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
0083|         return json.loads(result.stdout)["engine"]["version"]
0084| 
0085|     def report(self, result) -> str:
0086|         """The whole output of one run, wherever a line was written."""
0087|         return result.stdout + result.stderr
